title: Troubleshooting AI Import Failures
content: **List of Contents** Case 1 (There are Pattern points that are too close together) Case 2 (Pattern outlines are intersecting) Case 3 (This is an unsupported file type.) **Objective** Learn how to fix AI import failures respective to the types of error messages. **Case 1** ![Case_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018795768/Case_1.png) **Cause of Error:** When the points on the patterns are too close to each other. **Solution A - Delete & Join Points in Adobe Illustrator** 1. Open the file with issue in the Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find points too closed to each other and delete one of them. → As the point is deleted, the line is disconnected. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **Solution B - Adjust Pattern Size in CLO** 1. Navigate to the Main Menu and select File > Import > **Adobe (AI/PDF)**. → The Import AI/PDF window appears. 2. Deselect Auto Scale. 3. Increase the Scale percentage or select larger pattern unit and select OK. → The pattern file opens properly. **※ Note:** * If the pattern file still does not open properly, further increase the Scale percentage or select even larger pattern unit. Then, open the file again. * When the percentage and the unit is changed, the size of the pattern imported in CLO may differ from the original pattern size. **Case 2** ![Case_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703567/Case_2.png) **Cause of Error:** When the lines on patterns are intersecting. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find and edit the intersecting lines. 3. Save the file and re-open in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Case 3** ![Case_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703587/Case_3.png) **Cause of Error A:** When the Create PDF Compatible File option is not checked when saving the file in Adobe Illustrator. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Navigate to the Main Menu > File > Save as... 3. Assign the saving path and the file name. Then, click Save. 4. Check Create PDF Compatible File and click OK. 5. Reopen the file in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Cause of Error B:** When a line of a pattern is disconnected. ** Solution ** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find the disconnected pattern outline. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **※ Note: ** * For**Case 2** and **Case 3** , create a rectangle surrounding all patterns with issue, save in Adobe Illustrator, and then reopen in CLO as internal lines to open them without any pattern modification. * To use the Internal Lines as Patterns, use the [**Trace tool** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728) or the [**Clone as Pattern** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000343287)option to convert Internal Lines to Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides solutions for addressing common AI import failures in CLO3D by outlining specific error cases and their respective fixes.

title: CLO Under System Maintenance
content: CLO system maintenance is carried out to provide a seamless service for all of our users. Usually the entire process takes on average an hour. **W hat will be affected by system maintenance?** During maintenance, the items listed below might be unavailable. * Access to CLO software * CLO installer downloads * Sign-up (Email verification) * Change password * Sending Invoice * Subscription related emails **Will I be notified when system maintenance is completed?** Once the system is back, the CLO website banner will be back to normal. If this turns into an extended outage, we will update the status on [CLO social media channels](https://discord.gg/phNYjpj5VX). Should you have additional inquiries (or if you have trouble accessing CLO software or the installer download page after the website banner is restored) please [contact us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus). We apologize for any inconvenience caused, the CLO team is working to deliver a better user experience. CLO Support Team
content_description: This webpage provides essential information about scheduled CLO system maintenance, including potential service interruptions and updates for users.

title: Fill (ver 6.2)
content: **List of Contents** Duplicate Property ### **Objective** Create a realistic puffy garment by setting the fill type and weight. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VuJyDM7hYHs **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Fill** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409935066265/mceclip0.png) **Fill** **Operation** **Duplicate** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated.** ** 2. Click the piece to be applied or, Click anywhere in the 2D window ▶ Drag your cursor to select the pieces within the marquee. ** **→ The duplicated pieces appear on the mouse cursor. 3. Click the position where you place the duplicated piece. → The outlines of both pieces are sewn, and the internal lines crossed with them are sewn as well. → Display in purple. 4. Select any grey quilt lines to turn on the quilting effect. **Property** 1. Click the puffy pattern piece. **→** Filer Property appears in the Property Editor. 2. Once the puffy properties are set, simulate the garment.** ** **Property**** ** | **Description** ---|--- **Filer** | Type | Choose the type of filler. Weight | Enter the weight of the filler. **※Note:** Select multiple pattern pieces to set the total weight. The weight of each piece is calculated and distributed proportionally. Quilting Distance | Enter the quilting distance. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409111186457/mceclip2.png) **※Note:** Fill Volume is calculated based on the Quilting Distance and the Weight. Quilting Distance indicates the distance between the internal lines used as quilting lines, and you must input the distance value. If the internal lines are neither parallel nor their distance is constant, please enter the widest value. → You can have a reasonably realistic puffiness based on the pressure set by the weight and the quilting volume. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating realistic puffy garments in 2D design by detailing the fill properties, duplication process, and necessary settings for achieving desired puffiness.

title: [Property] Set Sublayer
content: ### **Objective** Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** → All established Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window. 2. Select the Sewing Lines to set Sublayer. → Sewing Line properties appear in the property editor. 3. Toggle on the **Set Sublayer** option. → A red arrow which indicates the order of the selected pair of Sewing Lines appear. **※ Note:** The half of the seam next to the arrow head is fixed and the other half next to the arrow tail moves according to the setting. 4. Change the Sublayer setting as needed. **Reverse Direction** | Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. ---|--- **Front** | **Back** | Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. 5. Activate **Simulation**. → Changes are applied respective to the setting.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for assigning orders to Sewing Lines on self-folding patterns to enhance simulation stability in sewing design.

Select a Start Menu folder. ![4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298687/4.png) 6. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. ![5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338888/5.png) 7. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. ![6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298667/6.png) 8. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. 9. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: [ ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)[![accpage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001356347/accpage.png) ](http://localhost:1947/)If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: [Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95)As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. ![configuration.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336948/configuration.png) 10. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. ![accesstoremote.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336928/accesstoremote.png) 11. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. 12. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. ![sentinelkey.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001337068/sentinelkey.png) **※ Note:** ** Identifying Server PC's IP Address ** Start (Windows) Button ▶ All Programs ▶ Accessories ▶ Command Prompt ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for installing the CLO Network Version of Windows (ver 5.0.0) while ensuring that assets from previous versions are retained.

title: Avatar Measure (ver 6.0)
content: **List of Contents** Basic/Surface Circumference Measure Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Height Measure ### **Objective** Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement 3D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360091740393/mceclip0.png) Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure ** Operation** **Basic/Surface Circumference Measure.** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. 3. Click once more when it is in the target shape. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. **Basic/Surface/Linear Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. → A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. → A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. (ver 6.0) **Height Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the point to be measured. → A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. **※ Note:** * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45˚ tilt. * Use [Attach to Measure](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426228-Attach-to-Avatar-Tape) tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. **Go back to the List of Contents**
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for accurately measuring the circumference, length, and height of an Avatar using basic and surface measurement tools.

title: Shirring (ver5.1.0)
content: ### **Objective** Express shirring realistically by reducing mesh size of the particular area of the Pattern. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LdaeKbFWgZ8 **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005494467/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern ▶** Select a Line**▶** Property Editor**▶** Selected Line**▶ Shirring**** ** **Operation** 1. Click on a Pattern Outline using the ![____3.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039919454/____3.jpg)**Transform Pattern** tool or ![____2.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360040742833/____2.jpg)**Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Follow the indicated path below: ** **Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶**Shirring **** ** 3. Click to toggle on the check box. → Shirring is applied to the selected line and the shirring symbol appears on the 2D Pattern. The result can be checked on the 3D Garment or on the 2D Pattern after switching the [2D Pattern Rendering Style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011148874-2D-Window-Display-Icons-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) to Mesh. 4. Adjust the **Interval** and **Height** of the Shirring. **Interval** | Adjust the distance between each mesh. ---|--- **Height** | Adjust the Height of the Shirring. ** ※Note:** Shirring is applied symmetrically when it is applied to Symmetric Patterns.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to realistically apply shirring to patterns in CLO 3D by adjusting mesh size, with visual aids and a helpful YouTube tutorial.

title: Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Move Rotate **Objective** Move or rotate slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move **** ** Operation** **Move** 1. [Create a zipper.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115004529388-%EC%A7%80%ED%8D%BC-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its **Gizmo** appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the **Gizmo** to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. **Rotate** 1. With the**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the **Gizmo** changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. **※ Note:** To reset slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select [**Reset Slider Arrangement**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-ua/articles/115004681608) option. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for adjusting the position and rotation of zipper sliders in a 3D garment design tool.

title: Edit 3D Pen (Garment)
content: **List of Contents** Select/Move Delete ### **Objective** Edit lines created on 3D Garments. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** **Select/Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** 2. Click the desired segment. → The selected segment is highlighted in yellow and its length appears (ver5.0.0.) 3. title: Register Custom OBJ as Button
content: Create Button OBJ Register Button OBJ Create Button OBJ by Thread Type ### **Objective** Register a custom OBJ file as Button. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0?si=H1MYv1aS1NI0W4RL&start=3417 **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Register Button ** Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024299748) ** Operation** **Create Button OBJ** Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. ** ※Required: ** ** ℹ️ From CLO 7.3, no 1, 2 requirements are not necessary and can be set at registration. ** * Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. e.g.) ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033429954) ![Button_OBJ.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033430114) Please check the attached OBJ file in your 3D modeling program for better understanding. ** ※Recommended: ** * Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. * The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in CLO. [ Button Property Setting ▶ Thread Length (cm)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005617768-%EB%8B%A8%EC%B6%94-%EC%86%8D%EC%84%B1-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95)) **Register Button OBJ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Register Button window appears. 2. After setting the following options, Click OK. **Property** | **Description****** ---|--- **Basic** | Set the name of the button file. **File** | **Size** | If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. **Size Name** | Set the size name. ** OBJ ** ** ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Select Mesh (ver 7.3) ** | Set the mesh for the buttons and thread. ** OBJ ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Width/Thickness** **/Weight** | Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. **Set as Default** | Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. **Axis Conversion (ver 7.3) ** | Switch axis of OBJ files in real time. **Preview (ver 7.3) ** | The imported OBJ file will be previewed. → The registered button is saved in the path below. CLO ▶ Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button **Create Button OBJ by Thread Type** 1. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to ***_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj.** 2. Register the created OBJ file as a button. 3. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. **C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button** 4. Run CLO and change the type of the thread in the button property window > Type > Thread Type.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for registering custom OBJ files as buttons in CLO, detailing the necessary requirements and step-by-step operations for successful integration.

title: Transform Graphic (3D)
content: **Transform Graphic (3D)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mRMopIL0VtA \- Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Material ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic (3D)** * **Scale Graphics ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFCd4pcwf-o \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The **Graphic Gizmo** will appear. \- Click and drag the arrow of the **Graphic Gizmo** to scale the selected Graphic. \- When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. - Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Graphic Transformation ▶ **Width** or **Height** to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to [Edit Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380188-Edit-Texture-3D-#Click4).) * **Rotate Graphics ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFCd4pcwf-o \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. \- Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. \- When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. * **Move Graphics** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Y6gCsykuaw \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the Graphic to move. \- When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.
content_description: Learn how to effectively scale, rotate, and move 3D graphics using the Transform Graphic tool in this comprehensive guide featuring helpful YouTube video tutorials.

title: Select
content: **List of Contents** Select Transform Pattern Tool Edit Pattern Tool Pattern Properties Deselect Select Multiple Patterns Select/Move Tool Select All **Select** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RVZ_gEcLxUg \- Select patterns in the 2D and 3D windows. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723988/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Transform Pattern Tool** * **Select with Clicks** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rXwmPDwV5Ek \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Hover over the pattern to be selected as its outline will be highlighted in light-blue. \- Click on the pattern. The Selected pattern will be highlighted in yellow. * **Lasso Selection** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hi0j5aA4YZo \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. \- Click the start point again to complete. \- Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. \- The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. **Edit Pattern Tool** * **Select with Clicks** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mGfEjXs3tpg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png)**Edit Pattern tool** , points and segments can be selected. Double click the point or the segment to select the entire pattern. * **Lasso Selection** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KNAjhDadlo8 ** \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. \- Click the start point again to complete. \- Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. \- The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. **Pattern Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GJo_0Qui9lc \- When the pattern is selected, its properties will appear in the **Property Editor**. **Deselect** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5NqubEWL9pA \- Click on the 2D window to **Deselect Patterns**. \- Originally selected patterns will no longer be highlighted in yellow. **Select Multiple Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=diQZIiqg1no \- To select multiple patterns, points, or segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select the items to be selected. **Select/Move Tool** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R5mPs3DIAXg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723988/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the 3D pattern to select and click on the 3D window to deselect. \- To select more than one patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and click on patterns to be selected. **Select All** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m0q-BOaaoVg \- To select all patterns in the 2D window, click and drag to encompass them with the marquee box. \- Or, hit the Ctrl+A keys on the keyboard to select all patterns in both 2D and 3D windows. \- When you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022663347/mceclip3.png) **Edit Sewing** tool is activated, all sewing lines will be selected. \- Likewise, when you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022725948/mceclip5.png) **Select/Move Button** tool is activated, all buttons will be selected in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for selecting and editing patterns in both 2D and 3D environments, featuring detailed instructions and helpful video tutorials.

title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
content: **Objective** Use the **Trace** function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. ** Location** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644128/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** 1.
